messages.subject: about how to use inla.posterior.sample()
parts:
Hi help,
 
I want to use inla.posterior.sample() to get some samples of the predictions... but I am not very clear about the outputs of the function..

My problem is like this: I have some observations at some locations, and I want the prediction at some other locations.. I use the joint process to call inla by stack two: est (with observations) and prd (for prediction)..
st.full <- inla.stack(st.dat,stkprd)
and call inla :
res <- inla(resp ~ -1 + intercept + f(i, model=spde2),
data=inla.stack.data(st.full),
control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(st.full), compute=TRUE))

The output of samp = inla.posterior.sample(1,res) has three lists .. one is 'latent' should be the samples I need.. but how can I extract them as sample of the predictions? I saw there are some values Predictor.XXXX, i.XXXX, and intercept.1... 
1.How can I get samples of the predictions according to my modle resp ~ -1 + intercept + f(i, model=spde2) ... 
2.I am not sure about -1 in resp ~ -1 + intercept + f(i, model=spde2) ... what does that mean? what about 0 (0 is used in the tutorial) am I wrong to use -1 here?

Thanks a lot!

messages.author: 573186f7652d8b08
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] about how to use inla.posterior.sample()
parts:
Hi Xiao,
I think you need to  add control.compute(, config=TRUE) in the inla call for you to use inla.posterior.sample( ) command . about -1,  we need to remove the automatically generated intercept given that we have already created one during model construction. Anyway, i also hope to hear from the experts this is just my view.

Erick.

On 13 November 2013 12:40, xiao guo <xiao.g...@gmail.com> wrote:
...
> 2.I am not sure about -1 in resp ~ -1 + intercept + f(i, model=spde2) ...
> what does that mean? what about 0 (0 is used in the tutorial) am I wrong to
> use -1 here?

As far as I know, "0" and "-1" are equivalent, and "-1" is quite ok to use.
As Erick said, it means "don't add an automatic intercept to the
model", and is needed to make sure that the intercept interacts in the
correct way with the "A" matrix.

Finn

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] about how to use inla.posterior.sample()
parts:
running the example on inla.posterior.sample()

example(inla.posterior.sample)

you got a 2 length list, because 2 samples is draw.

doing 1000 samples:
s1000 = inla.posterior.sample(1000,r)

we have an length 1000 output.
each of these 1000 elements has three values
one is the latent sampled field
s1000[[1]]$latent

to get it as a matrix, you can do
t(sapply(s1000, function(x) x$latent))
